etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French céleri, from Lombard sèller, from Latin selīnum, from Ancient Greek σέλῑνον (sélīnon). Displaced English march (“celery, smallage”) and smallage (“wild celery”).

definitions.definition: A European herb (Apium graveolens) of the carrot family.
(uncountable, vegetable) The stalks of this herb eaten as a vegetable.
A yellow-green colour, like that of a celery.
